all_posts.cooked:
Respected Sir,

I hope you are doing well. I want to write honestly about what I felt during the recent exam.

Sir, I am new to working fully inside the VM environment. I practiced very hard before the exam, but inside the exam hall the VM crashed at times and I became very confused. When pop-up messages came like “don’t worry if code is right it will be evaluated”, instead of giving me confidence, they made me doubt whether my work was really being counted.

In one AWK question, I submitted the same code twice — the first time it did not go through, the second time suddenly all test cases passed. Such things made me nervous and I kept questioning myself instead of focusing on solving.

Sir, I know many students are very skilled and can score 100, and I respect them. But for a student like me, who is trying with all sincerity, these technical issues reduced my confidence. I felt like my effort was wasted not because of lack of preparation, but because of the instability of the system.

I would even accept failure if it is due to my own mistakes. But it feels very discouraging when I suffer due to system crashes and confusing evaluation messages. That is why I wanted to share my feelings with you.

I humbly request you to kindly look into this issue for the sake of students like me who may not be perfect but are genuinely working hard to improve.

Thank you for reading this patiently, Sir.

Sincerely,

Akash

all_posts.name: Divyansh Gupta
all_posts.cooked:
Dear Sayn,

I hope this message finds you well. I am writing regarding the online proctored programming exam conducted on Saturday. While I understand that the grading document generally covers normal cases, the circumstances during the exam were unfortunately not normal for many of us.

The virtual machine provided for the exam was experiencing significant lag throughout the session. Even though the exam duration was extended by half an hour to accommodate this, the lagginess persisted and made it very difficult to attempt the paper with proper focus. In addition, some private test cases were failing due to issues such as “invalid literal” parse errors, despite all public test cases passing successfully. This inconsistency created further challenges during the assessment.

Given these circumstances, I kindly request some consideration so that our grades are not adversely affected. I completely understand that conducting a re-exam for all students would be challenging; however, possible alternatives could be either awarding a small bonus to account for these difficulties, or scheduling a re-exam for those who wish to improve.

If there is any doubt that these issues were experienced widely, you might also consider rolling out an exam feedback Google Form to gather inputs from students across the class. This way, you would receive collective feedback and not just isolated complaints.

I sincerely hope the faculty can consider this request, as the issues were genuine and made it difficult to perform to our full potential.

Thank you for your time and understanding.
